clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes—three cardinal features of metabolic syndrome—making it the most likely unifying diagnosis. Co‑existing anemia raises the possibility of iron‑deficiency, while the metabolic milieu predisposes to NAFLD, early CKD, and OSA. Other considerations (hypothyroidism, vitamin deficiencies, secondary hypertension, mood disorder) are less supported due to missing targeted investigations.
unresolved_findings: Fasting lipid panel (total, LDL, HDL, triglycerides) – needed to confirm metabolic syndrome criteria
Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4, anti‑TPO) – to evaluate hypothyroidism
Iron studies (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC, transferrin saturation) – to confirm/exclude iron‑deficiency anemia
Vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, homocysteine, folate levels – to assess combined deficiencies
Renal function (serum creatinine, eGFR) and urine albumin – to stage CKD
Sleep study or validated questionnaire – to diagnose OSA
Comprehensive menstrual history – to quantify potential iron loss
HIV/HCV serology – to rule out occult infection
recommended_workup: Thyroid panel (TSH, free T4, anti‑TPO antibodies)
Iron studies with ferritin and transferrin saturation
Serum vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, homocysteine, and folate levels
Serum creatinine, eGFR, and urine albumin/creatinine ratio
Overnight polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing
Abdominal ultrasound to assess hepatic steatosis and renal morphology
